title: Technical Panel Orchestration Script and Tribe Welcome Checklist
body:
Purpose and audience:
- Quick-run orchestration script for running high-throughput technical interview panels that double as a warm, consistent candidate experience and a smooth handoff into onboarding when we extend offers. Targeted at interview coordinators, hiring managers, panel leads, and people-ops partners.

High-level goals:
- Reduce candidate anxiety and variance across panels; make scoring comparable across interviewers.
- Make panel logistics predictable so SRE/eng time to schedule is minimized.
- Create a deliberate handoff path from offer -> preboard -> week1 so new hires feel immediate impact.

Before the panel (72–24 hours):
- Confirm panel roster: panel lead, timekeeper, tech deep-dive interviewer, systems design interviewer, culture-fit interviewer, optional hiring manager.
- Send panel brief (template below) to all interviewers and candidate: quick bios, role scope, must-ask probes, scoring rubric snapshot.
- Ensure candidate has a clear calendar invite with: dial-in + backup link, interviewer names & titles, expected duration + short agenda.
- Environment checks: interview VM or shared doc with coding prompt ready, Zoom/Meet links checked, recording disabled (unless candidate consent).
- People-ops: validate compensation band and tentative offer timeline with hiring manager; flagged exceptions noted in brief.
- Note to self (coord): confirm accessibility needs / timezone adjustments 48hrs out.

Panel day script (use verbatim bits for consistency):
- Host intro (0:00–0:02): "Hi — I'm {Panel Lead}, I'm coordinating today. We're excited to meet you. Today is ~60 minutes divided into three 18-minute segments + 6 min wrap. We'll introduce ourselves, then move into technical questions. Feel free to ask clarifying questions and think aloud. This is a conversation, not an exam"
- Candidate 2 min: invite candidate to give a quick personal intro and what they hope to learn from the conversation.
- Segment choreography:
  - Segment A — Systems/architecture (18 min): interviewer states the prompt, clarifies constraints, candidate ideates; scoring focus: capacity to reason about tradeoffs, clarity, and safety/operational considerations.
  - Segment B — Implementation/coding (18 min): interviewer gives a focused coding task; judge correctness, testability, and approach (not just passing tests). Pair-programming allowed.
  - Segment C — Product & culture fit (18 min): interviewer explores scope, collaboration, incident stories, and alignment with Redwood’s production-first thesis.
- Wrap (last 6 min): candidate Q&A, outline next steps and timeline. Panel lead closes with: "Thanks — we appreciate your time. We aim to share feedback/X next steps within Y days."

Scoring rubric (single page snapshot — use 1–4 scale):
- 4 = Exceeds expectations: clear, pragmatic tradeoffs, anticipates production constraints, solid communication, minimal coaching.
- 3 = Meets expectations: sound reasoning, minor gaps (edge cases), communicates effectively under pressure.
- 2 = Partial: requires multiple clarifying prompts, surface-level solutions, some unsafe assumptions.
- 1 = Not yet: incorrect core assumptions, not accountable to production constraints, major gaps.

Dimension definitions (brief):
- Problem decomposition: breaks complex requirements into testable pieces.
- Production thinking: attention to latency, cost, observability, failure modes.
- Implementation hygiene: readable code, tests or testable design, edge-case handling.
- Collaboration & communication: listens, asks clarifying q's, gives clear tradeoffs.
- Cultural fit signals: ownership examples, ops-first mentality, cross-team empathy.

Interviewer quick checklist (before each segment):
- State the prompt and constraints in 1 sentence.
- Ask candidate if they want clarifying questions.
- Timebox honestly; call for a brief synthesis at 12 minutes for long segments.
- Capture two signal notes: one technical highlight, one area of concern.

Post-panel debrief template (10–20 minutes max):
- Round-robin color: each interviewer provides 2 sentences aloud (green/yellow/red).
- Evidence log (one-liner each): key factual signals that support score.
- Consensus decision: Hire / No-hire / Hire-with-conditions. If no consensus, panel lead assigns tie-breaker (hiring manager).
- Operational actions: recruiter to send next-steps email within 48h (template included), hiring manager to approve comp for offers within 72h.

Offer -> preboard handoff (if decision = Hire):
- People-ops: create "offer packet" with role start-date options, typical week1 agenda, mentor pairing name, hardware preferences form.
- Manager: schedule a 30-min preboard welcome call (intro + expectation setting) within 5 business days.
- Engineering: create a stub ticket in onboarding-queue with account names, access list, slack channels to add.

Week0 (pre-start) welcome checklist (for candidate & internal):
- Candidate gets a welcome doc: what to expect first 30 days, key contacts, suggested pre-read (architecture overview, infra map).
- Hardware + credentials: confirm laptop spec + delivery windows; request KMS/HSM onboarding prerequisites if private deployment role.
- Slack invites & email alias created; manager picks first buddy.

Week1 plan (ops-first, measurable):
- Day 1: access, 1:1 with manager, desk setup, HR orientation, quick meet-the-team 15-min slots.
- Day 2–3: small engineering task with well-scoped repo + pairing session scheduled; objective: ship a tiny, observable change (monitoring hook or README improvement) by EOD day 3.
- Day 4–5: shadow rotations across infra/serving/runtime as relevant and retro on week0.

30 / 60 / 90 impact checkpoints (manager-led):
- 30d: contributor can produce a small PR end-to-end and own a bugfix; manager documents 3 learning goals; people-ops checks in on ramp signals.
- 60d: contributor leads a minor feature or owning a test/monitoring improvement; cross-team onboarding satisfaction > 70% (internal survey).
- 90d: contributor drives an initiative with measurable regression reduction or cost improvement; calibration note added to hiring rubric for future loops.

Templates appended (short forms to copy-paste) — paste these into calendar invites / emails:
- Panel brief subject line: "{Candidate} — Technical Panel (Role) — {Date} — Panel Brief"
- Quick candidate welcome snippet: "Thanks for taking the time — we’ll do a ~60min panel with three segments. Please join 10 minutes early to ensure no network issues. Here’s a single doc where prompts/questions will be shared."
- Debrief email timeline: "Internal decision recorded within 24–48h; candidate update within 48h. Offer target within 5 business days if green."

Known edge cases / open questions (notes to self):
- For senior IC loops (Principal+), consider separate rubric with strategic signals; current template may underweight cross-org influence.
- Need clear fallbacks for timezone-critical interviews (candidate in APAC) — propose two short panels instead of one long one.
- Accessibility: build explicit alt-flow for accommodations (longer breaks, alternative formats for whiteboarding).

Quick wins for adoption (ops rollout):
- Run a 4-week pilot with two hiring teams; collect interviewer feedback via a 5-question form.
- Ship a panel-brief generator in the recruiter UI that populates this script and the scoring sheet.

Appendix: one-paragraph rationale for engineering partners
- We hire for production-first judgment. Interviewers should bias to signals that correlate with early impact: can the candidate ship safe, observable changes that improve latency/cost/reliability? This script centers those signals and preserves human-centered candidate experience.

End notes: rough draft — please flag missing probes or uncomfortable questions. Current TODO: finalize single-page rubric PDF and add to handbook PR (linked above).
